title: Ryan Gosling’s ‘Ghost Rider’ Sets Release Date; Third Marvel Movie on 2028 Calendar
description: Disney has dated Ryan Gosling’s “Ghost Rider” movie for July 28, 2028, making it the third Marvel movie set for 2028. “Black Panther 3” is for Dec.
body:
Disney has dated Ryan Gosling’s “Ghost Rider” movie for July 28, 2028, making it the third Marvel movie set for 2028. “Black Panther 3” is for Dec. 15, 2028, while the as-yet untitled “X-Men” movie comes out on May 5, 2028. 

	The two titles were part of a large number of release updates made by the company in the wake of fan event D23, which took place this past weekend. Gosling’s role was announced in July at Comic-Con.


	An untitled Marvel movie is scheduled for Nov. 9, 2029; it was previously referred to only as an untitled Disney Movie. 
	

	The “Ghost Rider” movie is directed by Shawn Levy and written by “Star Wars: Starfighter” screenwriter Jonathan Tropper. Gosling takes over the role of the Spirit of Vengeance after Nicholas Cage played the motorcycle rider in two movies for Sony.

	Pixar’s “Ghost Market” will be released on March 10, 2028. The animated film is inspired by Asian myths of stores where the living and dead interact, and was originally set to be a streaming series before it was set as a theatrical release.

	“Coco 2” is set for Nov. 21, 2029. At D23, fans got a first look at the film’s central character Miguel, who is now a teenager. Benjamin Bratt reprises his role as Ernesto de la Cruz.

	“Tangled” will be released on March 31, 2028, and the animated movie “Clay” is set for Nov. 22, 2028.

	Other new dates include Searchlight horror film “Monitor,” which previously set for April 30, 2027, and moves up to April 16. Matt Black and Ryan Polly direct the story of a demonic entity that stalks message board moderators.

schema.headline: Ryan Gosling’s ‘Ghost Rider’ Sets Release Date; Third Marvel Movie on 2028 Calendar

title: CNN Correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister to Host Pre-Emmy Interview Series (TV News Roundup)
description:
CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister is set to host a special pre-Emmy interview series airing exclusively on CNN.

	“Coming Up” will see Wagmeist
body:
CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister is set to host a special pre-Emmy interview series airing exclusively on CNN.

	“Coming Up” will see Wagmeister sit down with Emmy nominees to discuss the stories behind the performances and achievements across their careers in television.

	The nominated stars include Colman Domingo (“The Four Seasons,” “Euphoria”), Paul W. Downs (“Hacks”), Allison Janney (“The Diplomat”), Katherine LaNasa (“The Pitt”), Ariana Madix (“Love Island USA”), Matthew Rhys (“Widow’s Bay,” “The Beast In Me”) and Jessica Williams (“Shrinking”).
	

	The interviews will roll out on CNN platforms during the Emmy voting window beginning Aug. 17. The final-round voting window ends Aug. 26, and the Emmy Awards ceremony is Sept. 14.

	
		FIRST LOOKS/TRAILERS	

	Prime Video has released first look images for “The Terminal List” Season 2, which premieres Oct. 21. 

	Based on Jack Carr’s best-selling novels of the same name, the sophomore season adapts the second book, “True Believer.” As Navy Seal Commander James Reece (Chris Pratt) battles dangerous forces, he travels across the globe in an attempt to find a new purpose after he finished his list, but a discovery in Moscow leaves him questioning his family’s history.

	Starring alongside Pratt are Tom Hopper, Constance Wu, Dar Salim, Luke Hemsworth, Gabriel Luna, Costa Ronin, Olga Kurylenko, Yul Vazquez, Martin Sensmeier, Arnold Vosloo and Shiraz Tzarfati. 

	Pratt also serves as executive producer with Carr, David DiGilio, Antione Fuqua, Kat Samick, Max Adams and Jared Shaw. 
	



	

									Marni Grossman/Prime
	





	

									Marni Grossman/Prime
	





	

									Justin Lubin/Prime
	





	

									Justin Lubin/Prime
	



	*

	“Victorious” is beginning a new chapter with “Hollywood Arts,” which premieres Oct. 15 on Netflix. 

	Trina Vega (Daniella Monet) is still a struggling actress who returns to Hollywood Arts, her former high school, “as an unqualified substitute teacher, quickly finding herself both clashing with and unexpectedly inspiring a new generation of ambitious and talented students as they learn to find their true path at Hollywood’s most elite performing arts school.”

	Starring alongside Monet are Alyssa Miles, Erika Swayze, Emily Liu-Wang, Peyton Jackson and Martin Kamm. Monet also serves as executive producer with Samantha Martin, Jake Farrow, Shauna Phelan and Jonathan Judge. 

	Watch the teaser trailer below.


	
		DATES	

	“Private Eyes West Coast” and Season 2 of “Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent” will premiere Oct. 5 on The CW.

	“Private Eyes West Coast” is a spin-off of the “Private Eyes” series, which ran for five seasons. The series sees Jason Priestley and Cindy Sampson reprise their roles as private investigators Matt Shade and Angie Everett. 

	The 10-episode season follows Shade and Angie as they settle into their new P.I. firm without their Toronto network.

	“Private Eyes West Coast” is executive produced by Priestley, Sarah Dodd, Jennifer Kassabian, Shawn Piller, Lloyd Segan, Jocelyn Hamilton and Darren Giblin. Dodd and Kassabian serve as showrunners.

	“Private Eyes West Coast” premieres Oct. 5 at 8 p.m. ET/PT.

	“Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent” returns for its second season with Detective Sergeants Henry Graff (Aden Young) and Frankie Bateman (Kathleen Munroe).

	Season 2 follows Graff and Bateman as they take on high-profile homicides inspired by some of Canada’s most infamous headlines. The cast also stars Karen Robinson as Inspector Vivienne Holness, K.C. Collins as Deputy Crown Attorney Theo Forrester, Nicola Correia-Damude as pathologist Dr. Lucy Da Silva and Araya Mengesha as tech expert Mark Yohannes.

	Based on the classic series format created by Dick Wolf and developed by Rene Balcer, “Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent” is produced by Lark Productions and Cameron Pictures in association with Universal Global Television. Tassie Cameron serves as showrunner and executive producer. Erin Haskett, Amy Cameron, David Valleau, Alex Patrick and Wanda Chaffey are also executive producers.
	

	“Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent” Season 2 premieres Oct. 5 at 9 p.m. ET/PT.
	
		EXECUTIVE NEWS	

	Tom Pelissero is set to join Netflix’s broadcast team as sideline reporter and NFL insider. He will also take a lead role in NFL coverage across several podcasts from Spotify’s The Ringer, including co-hosting “The Ringer NFL Show.”

	Pelissero joins Netflix’s broadcast team as sideline reporter across the streamer’s full slate of games this season. This includes the Rams-49ers game in Melbourne, Australia, the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game, a doubleheader Christmas Gameday and a Week 18 matchup on Jan. 9 in the final weekend of the regular season.

	For The Ringer, Pelissero will co-host “The Ringer NFL Show,” write about the NFL and appear on other shows, including every Thursday on “The Bill Simmons Podcast” during the NFL season.

	Pelissero was on the broadcast team in 2022 with Noah Eagle for the Vikings’ win over the Colts in the NFL’s biggest comeback in history. He served as NFL Network’s Senior Bowl sideline reporter from 2019 to July 2026.

title: CNN Has Prime-Time Anchors Locked In Ahead of Paramount Deal
description: Executives at Paramount Skydance have agreed to pay billions to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, but they may have to do a little more work if they w
body:
Executives at Paramount Skydance have agreed to pay billions to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, but they may have to do a little more work if they want to put their own stamp on the programming at CNN.

	CNN recently struck a new deal with Abby Phillip, anchor of the raucous 10 p.m. roundtable “NewsNight” that keeps al three of the anchors who host its primetime shows at the news giant for the foreseeable future, according to three people familiar with the matter. 
	

	Anderson Cooper, who anchors the 8 p.m. slot on CNN, renewed terms last year and it’s widely understood that Kaitlan Collins, who leads the “The Source” at 9 p.m. is working under a contract that has a few more years on left on it. Phillip is the last of the troika to renew alliances with the Warner Bros. Discovery news outlet.


	A CNN spokesperson said the network does not comment on contracts with talent.

	CNN was likely dealing with each anchor’s renewal as individual contracts opened, rather than deliberately planning a move to slow down a new owner’s plans.

	Nonetheless, having contracts in place could mean that Paramount will have to do some additional maneuvering if it wants to rework CNN’s programming lineup or rearrange the anchors who fill it. To be sure, a network can easily move an anchor if it wants — CNN forced Don Lemon to move out of his late-night roost on the schedule in 2022 to an ill-conceived morning-show concept after Warner was put under the control of CEO David Zaslav — but the new contracts mean that the anchors have some guarantees about the money they are owed in case changes are made.
	

	CNN staffers have been on edge as the Paramount deal moved closer to consummation. There is palpable concern that Paramount CEO David Ellison will assign oversight of CNN to Bari Weiss, a digital entrepreneur and opinion writer installed last year as editor in chief of CBS News. Her tenure at the news division has generated significant scrutiny and controversy, and has included the ouster of top producers and correspondents at the long-running newsmagazine “60 Minutes,” viewed for years as one of the jewels of the CBS lineup. There are growing fears within CNN that the Paramount acquisition would spur programming and talent changes that could be seen as being made to placate the Trump administration, rather than holding it to account. Inside CNN, there is a strong concern that Paramount’s executives “don’t know or don’t care” about managing the news giant for profit or for the future, according to one staffer. 

	All three anchors have taken on responsibilities beyond their evening-host duties. Cooper hosts the Sunday deep-dive program “The Whole Story” as well as “All There Is,” a podcast that examines grief. Collins anchors a primetime show while also working as the network’s chief White House correspondent. Phillip also hosts a Saturday-morning program, “Table for Five,” which, like “NewsNight,” is presented in a roundtable format. Phillip recently took up digital duties, hosting the new program “Confessions and Obsessions,” which focuses more on guests’ personal interests than their political leanings. 

	Signing Phillip to a new contract also means that CNN will likely rely heavily on the trio as the midterm elections approach. Elections can bring an injection of new viewership to news networks, as the drama around the race for federal office often lures people beyond CNN’s immediate crowd. CNN’s ad revenue is projected to increase about 4% to $510.4 million in 2026, according to Kagan, a market-research unit of S&P Global Intelligence, compared with $489.8 million in 2025.

schema.headline: CNN Has Prime-Time Anchors Locked In Ahead of Paramount Deal

title: How ‘Palm Royale’s’ All-Women Stunt Team Pulled Off That Catfight Sequence
description: AppleTV+’s “Palm Royale” made Emmy history when it landed nods for Outstanding Stunt Coordination for Comedy Programming (Mallory Thompson) and Outs
body:
AppleTV+’s “Palm Royale” made Emmy history when it landed nods for Outstanding Stunt Coordination for Comedy Programming (Mallory Thompson) and Outstanding Stunt Performance (Colby Lemmo and Sonja Wajih) for Episode 6, “Maxine Finds Herself.” It marked the first time an all-women stunt team from the same series has been concurrently nominated in both categories.

	In the episode, Claudia Ferri and Kristen Wiig go all out and get into a fight after Raquel (Ferri) pulls a gun on Maxine (Wiig). From trashing bedrooms and throwing couches, the pair tumbles down stairs and has a chase across the lawn before ending up in the pool. While most fights are typically 20 seconds, this lasts a full three minutes.
	

	Putting the episode’s stunt sequence together was exciting — particularly for Thompson, who said the script described the scene as a “Dynasty-style fight.” Thompson was familiar with the reference in which Alexis (Joan Collins) and Krystle (Linda Evans) get into a catfight and fall down the stairs of the Carrington Mansion. “Palm Royale” took things further.

	Speaking with Variety, Thompson says, “We got to pitch as many different crazy things as we could think.” Everything she pitched was approved by the episode’s director Stephanie Laing and showrunner Abe Sylvia.

	In putting it together, Thompson designed it with Wiig and Ferri in mind. “I knew that they both wanted to do so much,” she says.Thompson shot previs and used that as a map for when she would shoot with the actors and when the stunt doubles would step in. “Yes, it was very choreographed,” she says.
	

	The sequence took over four days to shoot because of the different locations and required over 60 setups. Wajih admits that when it came to the stair fall, she found the setup hilarious. “It’s always, Go fast, go hard, make it brutal.’ And you usually die at the end of a stair fall. But this was, ‘You’re going to go down with Colby, and you’re going to be entangled. It’s going to be a catfight brawl down the stairs.’”

	Wigs, wardrobe, long acrylic nails and jewelry — all needed to factor in, as both characters were the epitome of glamorous and flamboyant Florida socialites. Wajih says, “It was all kind of tricky because we started with a dive onto one another, and Colby and I hold on to each other, but have moments of flailing, but we’re also being mindful of not catching my heel in Colby’s cover-up, or not catching my ring in anyone’s wig, or in the stairs.” She adds, “It was a funny choreographic creative element to go down together, and also have all those elements to play with.”

	Lemmo points out that it wasn’t a simple staircase fall and was broken into three different steps because of how the stairs were designed. She also reveals where Wiig and Ferri actually intercut into the moment: “When they are coming toward camera, that’s them rolling and tumbling over each other, and then Sonja and I come down again.”

	As the two were entangled, Lemmo notes it was important to keep each other safe. “It was watching our heads. But when you’re that entangled, you don’t know which way is up, which way is down. Do I have Sonja’s leg? Do I have her arm? We got down to the bottom, and Sonja said, “I just needed to hold on to you. There’s no real planning of how it’s going to happen; you hold on, and tuck and roll, and you just go.”

	The fight didn’t end there; the pursuit continues with a chase across the lawn before they end up in the pool. Thompson says, “We pitched early on that we wanted to follow them into the water. That was a big ask because we have to get an underwater camera just for one shot, essentially, and but it just elevated it, and really brought it up to the ‘Dynasty’ level of ridiculousness.”

	A special underwater camera rig was set up to capture Lemmo and Wajih as they hit the water. But with other scenes needing to be filmed, it was left for last. Not only was the team losing light, but they had only one take. Thompson explains, “We had to get them coming out of the house, running across the lawn, and throwing her shoe.”
	

	But Lemmo and Wajih needed an audio cue. Once they had figured that out, Wajih notes, the key to the underwater stunt wasn’t just about wrestling. “I’m making sure not to drown Colby. She’s making sure not to drown me.”

	Watch the video below.

schema.headline: How ‘Palm Royale’s’ All-Women Stunt Team Pulled Off That Catfight Sequence

title: Music Industry Moves: iHeartMedia’s Alissa Pollack Named President of Mediabase
description: RCS Worldwide has announced the promotion of Alissa Pollack to president of Mediabase, a top music industry source for airplay analytics, chart inte
body:
RCS Worldwide has announced the promotion of Alissa Pollack to president of Mediabase, a top music industry source for airplay analytics, chart intelligence, and music data. In this elevated role, Pollack will also continue her full responsibilities as president of global music marketing at iHeartMedia.

	As president, Pollack will lead Mediabase’s strategic direction, global expansion, product innovation, and commercial growth, according to the announcement.
	

	Susan Larkin, RCS Worldwide president-CEO, said, “Alissa has spent her career at the intersection of music, data, and relationships, which is exactly where Mediabase lives. This promotion is a recognition of everything she has already built and a reflection of our confidence in where she will take Mediabase next. As she steps into this role she will have my full support as she leads Mediabase forward.”

	Pollack said, “I’m honored to lead Mediabase at such an exciting moment in its evolution while continuing the work I love at iHeartMedia. These roles are incredibly complementary because they share the same purpose: helping the industry make smarter decisions through meaningful insights.

	“As one of my first initiatives, I’m thrilled to make more Mediabase chart data publicly accessible through our newly updated Mediabase.com site. Music fans, industry professionals, and artists can now view the Top 50 charts across every format in both the U.S. and Canada, providing greater visibility into music performance and trends across North America.”

	+ Valerie Pensa, a multipl Clio Award winner who most recently was head of marketing at RCA Records, has left the company to launch of new venture Moonstruck Management & Marketing Inc., which is based in Los Angeles. Over the years she has worked closely with such artists as Tate McRae, P!nk, Doja Cat, Miley Cyrus, Sia, Lisa and more.
	

	Pensa said, “Moonstruck means dreamily entranced — devoted to something you believe in. That’s exactly how I feel about artists with real vision, and it’s the only way I know how to work. This industry doesn’t sit still and my job is to stay dedicated to that vision no matter how the business evolves.”

	+ Jet Management, the Venice, CA-based music management focused on dance music, has announced a new joint management partnership with Debonair (DBNR), the Belgium-based boutique music management company, launching with the acclaimed French electronic music duo Polo & Pan, who are currently on a North American tour as the support act for Jet Management act Empire of the Sun. DBNR’s roster also includes Charlotte de Witte, Enrico Sangiuliano, Bazart and Oliver Symons; Jet’s also manages Justice, Foster the PeopleSam Gellaitry, Neil Frances, WhoMadeWho and others; it is also a partner of the company Firebird.

	“I’ve been a longtime fan of Polo & Pan and genuinely enjoyed their records and live shows long before this collaboration came together,” said DBNR founder-CEO Alexander Vandriessche.  “We’ve always had a lot of respect for what Jet built and how they approach artists globally, and with Polo & Pan and this new partnership, there was a very organic fit between both teams and it felt like the right project to start building something together.”

	Jet co-founder Tyler Goldberg added, “We are thrilled for the opportunity to both work with one of the most creative and talented artists in the world, one which we’ve admired for years, and to partner with one of the best managers in our industry, our dear friend Alexander Vandriessche.”

	+ Mom+Pop Music has signed singer-songwriter Crash the Party. Signed by label co-founder Michael Goldstone and Katie Fagan, the artist has released the song “Cold Feet” to launch the partnership.

	Crash the Party says, “Growing up in rural Georgia, pursuing music sometimes felt a little delusional. I knew I wasn’t meant to work in a factory, lay cable, or follow the paths a lot of my neighbors took — I just knew I had to make music. Being with Mom+Pop is truly a dream, and it feels like validation that I’m on the right path, crazy or not!” More music will be released later in the fall.
	

	+  Fenix Entertainment has announced a global partnership with Maluma to lead the development and strategy behind his upcoming world tour, taking place in 2027 and 2028.The 35-year-old company currently works with Luis Miguel, Ricardo Arjona, and Ricardo Montaner, while also developing strategic partnerships with Shakira across multiple markets.

	Marcelo Fígoli, founder and president of Fenix Entertainment, said: “Working with an artist with Maluma’s career and international reach is both a challenge and an enormous responsibility. We believe in his vision, his talent, and the exciting moment he is experiencing in his career. We are incredibly proud to be part of this new chapter and to put our team and experience behind a project of this scale.”

	+ Warner Records Nashville has reshaped its marketing team structure with the announcement of several staff promotions and newly created roles:

	Addison Nunes is being promoted to VP of marketing where she will oversee marketing duties for one half of the roster alongside Anna Pittman, who will lead marketing efforts for one half as well, continuing her role as VP of marketing.

	Justin Luffman will move into the newly created role of VP of culture & creative marketing. In this role, he will act as a driving force behind our artists’ identities and cultural relevance, according to the announcement.

	Pittman will be supported by Jackson Ammons, who moves into his new role as marketing manager. Nunes is supported by new hire Jennipher Miller, who begins her new role as marketing manager, while Samantha Nepsa assumes Nunes’ previous duties with her promotion to senior analyst of data & analytics.

	Allyson Kim will move into the role of manager of touring & fan activations, while Alyssa Cohen joins the marketing team as coordinator, reporting to EVP of marketing Victoria Mason.

	+ United Talent Agency announced today the addition of six new executive appointments, along with 11 internal promotions across the music division. The announcement is the latest in a series of advancements for the department, including the recent elevation of James Wright to co-head of U.K. music, the announcement of seven new music partners in March, and the promotion of 19 colleagues in December.
	

	Chris Anderson (Agent), Randy Freedman (Agent, Music Brand Partnerships), Jordan Golenberg (Agent), and Lauren Katzakian (Executive, Business Affairs) are based out of Los Angeles. Anderson joins UTA following nearly two decades in artist management and talent representation. With over a decade of experience at Universal Music Group and elsewhere, Katzakian is the newest member of the UTA Business Affairs team focusing on touring and Music Brand Partnerships. Freedman also arrives via UMG, and will focus his efforts within the Music Brand Partnerships division. Golenberg joins from Day After Day Productions role.

	Anthony Brown (Agent) and Becky Drouet (Agent) join the ranks of agents in London. Brown brings over 13 years of industry experience from CAA, where he specialized in hip-hop and R&B. Drouet will work across touring and corporate/private group, following more than 18 years at LPO.

	UTA’s newest coordinator class will support agents and executives across several divisions within the music department, including touring, marketing, brand partnerships, music crossover, A&R and more. Juan Aguirre, Lindsey Cole, Alia Lopotanak and Mark Soleymani are the newest coordinators in the Los Angeles office; Julian Huff, Pearse Matteson, and Jenna Shatzman have been upped to coordinators in New York; Cat Ingersoll is the latest to be elevated to coordinator in Nashville; and Dylan Bryant, Brooke Newton and Emily Rhodes are the latest coordinator elevations in London.

title: Peacock Launches Test of Membership Rewards Program With Perks Including NBCU and Bravo Merch Discounts, Free Pizzas
description: NBCUniversal‘s Peacock launched a limited new membership program in a beta test with a variety of perks — aimed at keeping them from flying the coop
body:
NBCUniversal‘s Peacock launched a limited new membership program in a beta test with a variety of perks — aimed at keeping them from flying the coop as streaming subscribers.

	The test of Peacock’s membership program is available initially to a limited, “randomly selected” group of Peacock Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, according to NBCU. “Through a mix of NBCUniversal benefits, partner offers and exclusive experiences, the program will recognize and reward Peacock subscribers, deliver added value, and create deeper connections to the fandoms that power NBCUniversal,” the company said.
	

	NBCU’s test of the Peacock rewards program follows similar efforts by other streamers, including Disney+ Perks, which offers its customers an array of different promotional offers and discounts.


	Launched in July 2020, the Peacock streaming service turned its first-ever quarterly profit for Q2 2026. Peacock paid subscribers totaled 48 million as of the end of June, gaining 2 million net additions during the period.

	As Peacock continues to test and evolve the program, NBCU said, additional rewards are expected to be added over time, including Universal Parks perks and experiences, NBCU content previews and early access to NBCU live events.

	On a recent episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, Matt Strauss, chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group, spoke about the Peacock membership program. “[W]e’re starting to evolve from thinking of this as streaming to entertainment, from subscription to membership,” he said. “Again, we’re always charting out what we see as the next white space. This is where we see, at least for NBCUniversal, the next wave of growth for streaming and the broader business as we’re continuing to build out where we see the big opportunity.”
	

	During the beta test, Peacock’s membership program will group participants in three tiers based on their tenure as subscribers: Gold (3 months-1 year), Platinum (1-3 years) and Diamond (3+ years), with select rewards tailored to each tier.

	At launch, members in the beta will have access to the following rewards: 


An NBCU Shop 25% discount (for Shop at NBC Studios products)
A Bravo Shop discount (dependent on membership tier), with Gold members eligible for 15% off, Platinum members receiving 20% off and Diamond members receiving 25% off
A complimentary one-year Instacart+ membership (which auto-renews as a paid membership after 12 months); benefits include no grocery delivery fees on orders of at least $10, a subscription to New York Times Cooking at no additional cost (if activated by May 6, 2027) and free family sharing with up to three people
A Pizza Hut digital code that allows them to buy one menu-priced medium pizza and get a second medium pizza of equal or lesser value free (limited time offer; offer is unlocked after streaming three movies)

schema.headline: Peacock Launches Test of Membership Rewards Program With Perks Including NBCU and Bravo Merch Discounts, Free Pizzas

title: BINI, SB19 and Lea Salonga Lead ‘Forgotten Island’ Soundtrack (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The full track listing for Dreamworks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” has been revealed.

	SB19, BINI and Lea Salonga are among the artists leading t
body:
The full track listing for Dreamworks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” has been revealed.

	SB19, BINI and Lea Salonga are among the artists leading the soundtrack. As previously revealed, H.E.R. and Katseye’s Sophia Laforteza also feature. The soundtrack will be released on Sept. 18 with the film set to open on Sept. 25.

	The film follows H.E.R. and Liza Soberano as the voices of Jo and Raissa, two best friends who embark on one last adventure together. Their journey takes them into a night filled with shapeshifters, demons and witches, testing their friendship as they struggle to find their way out of a magical portal and return home.
	

	The music in the film blends influences from the 1980s and ’90s, particularly drawing inspiration from Filipino and Filipino-American musical culture. 

	“Forgotten Island” also features a remixed version of INXS’ classic “Never Tear Us Apart,” sung by Katseye’s Sophia Laforteza, for an emotional moment between the two friends.

	The film’s two female leads, H.E.R. and Soberano, are at the helm of the film’s title track “BRB.” Filipino boy band SB19 will cover the classic song “Mga Kababayan” by Francis M. Additionally, Ruby Ibarra and Carl Angelo perform “Salbahe Ako.”

	The film is scored by composer Nathan Matthew David who leaned heavily on analog synths from that era. Speaking about the score, David said, “There are elements of ’80s pop and hip-hop. But when the girls stumble into the mystical portal and end up on the island of Nakali, “the story evolves, and so does the sound.” 
	

	He also introduces music and instruments from indigenous Filipino tribes, utilizing traditional Filipino instruments like chanters, the Las Piñas bamboo pipe organ, and a Filipino choir singing Tagalog phrases.

	In the film, Salonga plays a dreaded Salonga’s mythical creature. For that, he used the talking gong, known as the indigenous gandingan, a traditional instrument of the southern Philippines.

	How did directors Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado get Salonga to play a villain? Crawford revealed that they sent a pitch to see if she was interested. “We heard from her team right away.”

	Salonga said yes, but the directors realized that, as amazing as the part was, they were concerned it wouldn’t be meaty enough for her. Mercado said, “She was already on the same page as us, understanding that the Manananggal didn’t need to speak a lot to be scary.”

	“She elevated the material,” Mercado said. He went on to explain that Salonga found the voice for the character after listening to H.E.R. and Soberano. “She said, ‘I’ll change my voice so that it complements theirs. If they’re a little higher, then I’ll make the Manananggal deeper and speak from the gut.’” Salonga’s vocals are used throughout David’s score. The album can be preordered here. 	Joining the HBO finance industry drama are: Cary Elwes (“Dead Man’s Wi
body:
The fifth and final season of “Industry” is adding seven new cast members. 

	Joining the HBO finance industry drama are: Cary Elwes (“Dead Man’s Wire,” “The Princess Bride,” “Robin Hood: Men in Tights”), Dianna Agron (“Glee,” “Shiva Baby”), Sam Riley (“Mint,” “Islands”), Jessica Brown Findlay (“Silo,” “Peaky Blinders”), Luke Manley (“Marty Supreme”), Bally Gill (“Slow Horses,” “Interview with the Vampire”), and Eduard Poliakov (“On Drive,” “Mavka: The True Myth”). 
	

	Elwes will play Padgett Stillman, an investor. Agron will play Skip Binksy, the CFO of a wellness tech company. Riley will play Solomon Kerr, described as “an elusive British businessman who made his fortune in Silicon Valley.”


	Brown Findlay will play Marina St. Clair, said to be “a family friend of Sir Henry Muck (Kit Harington).” Manley will appear as Stevie Delmonte, an execution trader. Gill play Nikesh Shah, described as “a charismatic left-wing politician.” And Poliakov will play Olexij Kovalchuk, a trader. 

	As previously announced, Season 5 of “Industry” will be the show’s last. The series’ cast also includes: Myha’la, Marisa Abela, Kit Harington, Ken Leung, Max Minghella, Miriam Petche, Sagar Radia, Toheeb Jimoh, Charlie Heaton, Amy James-Kelly, Roger Barclay, Andrew Havill, Kiernan Shipka, Kal Penn, Jack Farthing, Stephen Campbell Moore, Claire Forlani, and Edward Holcroft.

	Zosia Mamet is also set to appear in Season 5, which is now in production in the UK. 

	“Industry” is created, written, and executive produced by Mickey Down & Konrad Kay. The series is a Bad Wolf Production for HBO/BBC and is executive produced by Jane Tranter, Kate Crowther, and Ryan Rasmussen for Bad Wolf; Kathleen McCaffrey for Little Gems; and Rebecca Ferguson for BBC. Directors for Season 4 included Down & Kay, Michelle Savill, and Luke Snellin. Writers include Down, Kay, and Joseph Charlton.
	

	Elwes is repped by Link Entertainment and Independent Artists Group. Agron is repped by Paradigm & Hansen Jacobson. Riley is repped by Independent Talent and Tapestry London. Brown Findlay is represented by Tapestry. Manley is repped by Authentic Talent & Literary Management. Gill is repped by JAG. Poliakov is repped by R Talent. 

	(Pictured, left to right: Cary Elwes, Jessica Brown Findlay, Dianna Agron, Sam Riley, Luke Manley, Bally Gill, Eduard Poliakov)

schema.headline: ‘Industry’ Season 5 Adds Seven to Cast, Including Cary Elwes, Jessica Brown Findlay, Dianna Agron

title: Taylor Swift Praises Phoebe Bridgers’ New Album ‘Lost Weekend,’ Calls It an ‘Absolute Triumph in Every Way’
description: Taylor Swift has spoken out about her love of Phoebe Bridgers‘ new album “Lost Weekend,” praising the singer-songwriter for her “absolute triumph” o
body:
Taylor Swift has spoken out about her love of Phoebe Bridgers‘ new album “Lost Weekend,” praising the singer-songwriter for her “absolute triumph” of a record.

	Swift, who previously featured Bridgers on her 2021 song “Nothing New,” took to Instagram Stories to congratulate her on her latest project. “It’s her birthday but she gave us a gift,” wrote Swift. “Haven’t been able to stop listening. This album is an absolute triumph in every way.”
	

	She went on to praise the songwriting on “Lost Weekend” and wished her a happy birthday. “To write about grief with such vulnerability and detail, and to trust the listener with this much honesty,” she continued. “Happy bday @phoebebridgers I love you!!”


	Swift previously tapped Bridgers for “Nothing New,” a vault track included on “Red (Taylor’s Version).” During an interview with Billboard at the time, Bridgers reflected on the experience and described it as a “dream.” “I just am so excited to have people take it at face value the day that it comes out, because I got teary recording it. I just couldn’t be more excited,” she said. “I think that she is an incredible businessperson and an incredible writer. What she’s been able to build just from writing adeptly from a young age is insane.”

	Bridgers would continue on to serve as an opening act on a handful of Swift’s Eras Tour shows in Nashville, Philadelphia and more in 2023. This past weekend, Bridgers and Swift attended the wedding of recording engineers Laura Sisk and Oli Jacobs in the U.K.

title: Paramount Requests States and WGA Be Required to Post $1.9 Billion Bond to Cover Financial Losses While Warner Bros. Merger Is Stuck on Hold Pending Trial
description: David Ellison’s Paramount Skydance asked the judge overseeing the antitrust lawsuits filed by 12 states and the WGA to force the plaintiffs to pony
body:
David Ellison’s Paramount Skydance asked the judge overseeing the antitrust lawsuits filed by 12 states and the WGA to force the plaintiffs to pony up a whopping $1.88 billion bond to cover the company’s losses related to the delay in its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.

	Paramount filed the motion Monday with Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin, who has scheduled a trial start date of March 2, 2027. The $1.88 billion would be payable to Paramount in the event Paramount prevails in the antitrust litigation. 
	

	Paramount “hereby moves this Court for an order modifying the Stipulation and Order Not to Close, Dkt.170, to require dissolution of that order unless Plaintiffs post a $1,884,726,092.73 bond by September 30, 2026,” the company said in the motion. The company said the court-approved order not to close the Paramount-Warner Bros. deal — which Paramount agreed to — “inflicts substantial costs on Paramount, which is otherwise poised to consummate the merger.”


	In a statement to Variety, a representative for Paramount said, “Today, Paramount requested that the court enforce the statutory requirement that the plaintiffs post a bond in connection with their pending litigation, which blocks us from closing our merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.”

	Variety has reached out to the California Department of Justice and the WGA for comment on Paramount’s motion.

	The 12 states, led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, sued in federal court in July to block Paramount’s $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. The states allege the proposed merger will illegally reduce competition in the markets for theatrical and blockbuster films, as well as basic cable TV. The Writers Guild of America filed its own suit, arguing that the deal also will illegally reduce the number of buyers for writers’ work. 
	

	Paramount agreed to put the merger on hold until the trial concludes, after Martinez-Olguin granted a temporary restraining order to pause the deal for 28 days. In granting the TRO, Martinez-Olguin waived a bond requirement because “Plaintiffs have demonstrated that Plaintiff States bring suit to enforce important public interests.”

	The antitrust lawsuit by the states and WGA are the only barriers remaining to the closing of the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, which has received regulatory clearances from 68 jurisdictions.

	Paramount execs were confident its deal for Warner Bros. would easily clear regulatory hurdles by the third quarter of 2026. Indeed, as a sweetener in its bid for WBD, Paramount added a provision that requires it to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders a “ticking fee” amounting to roughly $7 million per day, starting Oct. 1, until the merger closes. That would total $1.3 billion by the time the trial is scheduled to conclude in March 2027.

	Paramount is seeking a bond “based on the straightforward calculation of the maximum potential ticking consideration and financing costs from this litigation,” the company spokesperson said. “But these are not the only costs of delay. By virtue of what will be at least an eight-month delay in closing, there will be no integration and no ramped-up investment in content, production and creative talent by the combined company. Of course, in addition, employees of both Paramount and WBD are also harmed by the uncertainties caused by the delay.”

	Based on the number of Warner Bros. shares outstanding, the ticking fee Paramount is obligated to pay will be approximately $6.97 million per day, or $1.69 billion for the period from Oct. 1, 2026, to June 1, 2027, per Paramount’s motion. In addition, Paramount would incur $190 million in “incremental financing costs that arise from delaying consummation of the merger until June 2027,” the company said in the filing.

	According to Paramount, the Clayton Act — the federal antitrust law on which the lawsuits by the states and WGA are based — and other federal laws “expressly provide that plaintiffs are required to post a bond covering the potential harm from halting a transaction to litigate, so that if they lose, the injured party has a source of recovery for the damage caused.” In the case of the Paramount-WBD merger, “every month of delay carries substantial and quantifiable financial consequences,” the company rep said.
	

	California’s Bonta has said repeatedly that the states are focused on winning at trial rather than reaching a settlement, and that Paramount’s proposed conditions do not go nearly far enough to address the anticompetitive concerns raised in the lawsuit. Bonta has argued that “behavioral” remedies — such as promises to release a certain number of films — have proven ineffectual in the past, and has said that he is focused on structural changes that Paramount has been unwilling to make.

	Bonta, asked about a potential settlement Monday on MS Now’s “State of Play With Peter Alexander,” said that “we prefer to resolve disputes in the boardroom, not the courtroom, if possible.”

	“And so coming to the table in this case in good faith to sincerely discuss how to resolve this case has always been on the table and remains on the table,” Bonta said. “But Paramount, Warner Bros. breaking the law and expecting us to let them get away with it, that is not on the table and never will be on the table. And that’s essentially what they’re asking for right now.”

	In Paramount’s statement Monday, the company spokesperson said, “We remain confident that plaintiffs’ case is without merit and will defend our pro-competitive transaction in court. We look forward to closing this transaction and delivering its benefits to consumers and entertainment industry workers in California, the United States and around the world.”

	Separately, eight state attorneys general, including California’s Bonta, in March sued to block Nexstar’s acquisition of TV station group rival Tegna on antitrust grounds. In April, they won a court preliminary injunction halting the companies from continuing with their merger integration. U.S. District Court Judge Troy Nunley of California’s Eastern District, in his ruling granting the preliminary injunction, noted that courts have “issued bonds in nominal amounts where a state is advocating for the public interest.” He wrote that “the Court finds it appropriate to require Plaintiffs to post a nominal bond in the amount of $10,000.”

title: Baby Gabriel's Biological Parents Authorize Heart Surgery After Initially Wanting Abortion
description:
Baby Gabriel's Biological Parents
                          Authorize Heart Surgery to Save Him
body:
Baby Gabriel's Biological Parents
                          Authorize Heart Surgery to Save Him
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 17, 2026
                            12:37 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The biological parents who wanted their surrogate to terminate the pregnancy are now taking steps to keep their newborn alive ... telling a judge they've decided their son will undergo major heart surgery.
      
    
            According to a court filing, obtained by TMZ, Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed have elected to have the baby undergo the Norwood procedure after consulting with doctors at Children's Health.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Norwood procedure is a complex open-heart surgery performed on newborns with hypoplastic left heart syndrome -- the condition doctors discovered during the pregnancy. It helps the side of the heart that works pump blood through the body.
      

            The parents call their son Rumi in the filing. Surrogate McKenna West referred to him as Gabriel ... though Nausheen and Omar say that is not his name.
      
    
            The filing does not reveal when the operation will take place, but the parents say they will provide the date privately if the court requests it.
      
    
            As we reported ... after doctors discovered the heart defect at the 20-week scan, Nausheen and Omar invoked a clause in the surrogacy agreement requiring West to terminate the pregnancy.
      
    
            West initially scheduled the procedure ... then changed her mind and traveled from Alaska, where she lives, to Texas, where she gave birth early last week.
      
    
            The biological parents have since obtained a restraining order, giving them medical decision-making authority. The order also bars West from making medical decisions or interfering with their access to the baby.
